error-named-but-no-correction-when-knowa: A form says what's wrong ('Invalid date') but never tells you how to fix it, even though the correct format or rule is clearly knowable.
suggestion-present-but-wrong-or-misleadi: A form gives a specific fix-it suggestion, but it's factually wrong for the field, so even following it the input still gets rejected.
suggestion-correctly-withheld-security-p: For a security-sensitive field like a password, giving only a generic error and no specific fix is correct to avoid leaking information, so it shouldn't be flagged as a failure.
correction-not-knowable-dna-pass: For a free-text field where the system genuinely can't know the right answer, offering only a generic message is fine and shouldn't be penalized for lacking a suggestion.
suggestion-present-but-too-vague-to-be-a: An error message gestures at fixing ('Please check your entry') but is too generic to tell you what to actually change, so you still can't correct the input.
suggestion-stranded-far-from-field-or-un: A correct fix-it suggestion exists but is placed far from its field with no link or proximity, so you can't find it or connect it to the field that needs fixing.
color-asterisk-icon-only-no-text-suggest: A field's error and how to fix it are conveyed only by colour, a red asterisk, or an icon, with no text describing the correction, so a screen-reader user gets no guidance.
